title: Zelensky Publishes Open Letter to Putin — Proposes Immediate Ceasefire + Face-to-Face Meeting; Kremlin Says Putin 'Can Come to Moscow Any Time' — Day 1,561
detail: On June 4, 2026 — Day 1,561 of Russia's full-scale invasion — President Zelensky made the most significant Ukrainian diplomatic move since the Geneva talks of February 2026: he published an open letter directly addressed to Vladimir Putin. The letter proposed three specific steps: (1) an immediate full ceasefire along the current frontline for the duration of negotiations; (2) a face-to-face bilateral meeting in a neutral third country — with Switzerland, Turkey, or an Arab state specifically named as acceptable venues; (3) an all-for-all prisoner-of-war exchange as a confidence-building starting point. Zelensky's framing was direct: 'Enough of the war.' The letter came days after Russia's devastating June 2 mass strike (73 missiles + 656 Shaheds; 17–18 killed nationwide; Kyiv building collapsed) and Ukraine's own June 3 deep-strike on St. Petersburg during SPIEF. The Kremlin's response was delivered by spokesman Dmitry Peskov, who confirmed Putin had seen the letter but had not yet formally read it. Peskov added that Zelensky 'can come to Moscow any time' — a venue Zelensky had explicitly and publicly ruled out. Bloomberg characterized the letter as a significant shift in Ukrainian diplomacy; the Kyiv Independent described it as Zelensky 'throwing down the gauntlet.' The US-brokered Geneva framework talks remained deadlocked over territorial arrangements, with a June 2026 target for a deal having passed without agreement.

media.caption: Zelensky's open letter to Putin proposes immediate ceasefire, bilateral meeting in neutral country — June 4, 2026

title: Russian Drone Strikes Multi-Story Residential Building in Kharkiv — Two Districts Targeted — Day 1,561
detail: On June 4, 2026 — Day 1,561 of Russia's full-scale invasion — Russian forces launched drone strikes on two districts of Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city. One drone struck a multi-story residential building, causing a fire. Ukrainian emergency services responded to the blaze; casualties were not immediately confirmed in early reports. The strikes on June 4 continued a pattern of near-daily Russian drone and bomb attacks on Kharkiv, which has been under Russian aerial assault throughout the war due to its proximity (approximately 40 km) to the Russian border and its significance as Ukraine's industrial and cultural capital in the northeast. Separately, ISW confirmed that neither Russian nor Ukrainian forces made confirmed territorial advances anywhere along the frontline on June 4, with the Pokrovsk, Huliaipole, Lyman, and Kupiansk sectors all recording combat engagements but no net movement.

media.caption: Russian drone strikes Kharkiv multi-story residential building as two city districts are targeted — June 4, 2026

title: Ukraine Strikes Svetlyak-Class Patrol Ship in Occupied Crimea + Gunpowder Plant Inside Russia — Day 1,561
detail: On June 4, 2026 — Day 1,561 of Russia's full-scale invasion — Ukrainian forces conducted multiple overnight offensive operations against Russian military targets. Ukrainian forces struck and damaged a Russian Svetlyak-class border patrol ship in occupied Crimea, continuing Ukraine's sustained campaign to degrade Russia's Black Sea and coastal fleet assets. Separately, Ukrainian drones struck a gunpowder plant and military storage facilities inside Russian territory. These strikes were part of the continuous retaliatory operations Ukraine has maintained throughout June 2026 even as its cities and civilian infrastructure endure Russian mass barrages. Combined with the June 3 strikes on St. Petersburg's oil terminal and the corvette Boikiy at Kronstadt, and the June 2 strikes on the Ilsky refinery and Pantsir-S1 system, Ukraine has maintained a high operational tempo of deep-strike missions into Russian-controlled territory throughout the first week of June 2026.

media.caption: Ukraine strikes Svetlyak-class patrol ship in occupied Crimea and gunpowder plant inside Russia — June 4, 2026

title: Ukrainian MoD: 1,300 Russian Troops Eliminated in 24 Hours — Cumulative Losses Reach ~1,369,340 — Day 1,561
detail: On June 4, 2026 — Day 1,561 of Russia's full-scale invasion — Ukraine's General Staff reported approximately 1,300 Russian personnel eliminated in the preceding 24 hours, bringing cumulative losses since February 24, 2022 to approximately 1,369,340 personnel (killed, wounded, missing combined — Ukrainian estimate). The 1,300 daily figure on June 4 is higher than June 3 (1,130) and reflects continued high-intensity fighting across multiple frontline sectors despite ISW's assessment of no confirmed territorial advances by either side on June 4. The daily attrition figures for early June 2026 — averaging ~1,300+ per day — reflect Russia's sustained offensive pressure in the Pokrovsk, Huliaipole, Lyman, and Kupiansk directions, as well as casualties from Ukraine's deep-strike campaign which continues to target Russian logistics, air defense, and industrial facilities deep inside Russia.

media.caption: Russian cumulative losses reach ~1,369,340 with 1,300 eliminated in 24 hours — Day 1,561, June 4, 2026
